tasks.short: Manage unit staff, budgets and goals

steps.what: Review unit staffing, spending and capacity information and clarify missing management context
outputs: checked unit management picture and unresolved information gaps

steps.what: Develop unit budget, operating plans and long-range goals with responsible stakeholders
inputs: checked unit management picture and unresolved information gaps
outputs: unit plans and budget decisions within delegated authority

steps.what: Manage unit staff and coordinate implementation, resolving resource conflicts and operational concerns
inputs: unit plans and budget decisions within delegated authority
outputs: coordinated unit operations and escalated resource decisions

tasks.design: Configure an existing management view {BI} over authorised roster {HCM} and expense {ERP} records. It reduces locating and aligning existing totals while the nurse manager retains missing-context checks, budgeting, staff discussions and operational decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Management review may require manually aligning existing roster and spending views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reporting can group existing records by unit and period without ranking workers or recommending clinical staffing decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Balance service needs, resources and staff concerns under changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Understand context behind totals and negotiate practical priorities.
tasks.altitude: Less routine information assembly with retained management responsibility.

reach.task: Clarify unit spending and budget constraints
reach.learn: Which costs require interpretation before planning

evidence.claim: A native unit management view is an E1 design proposal; this digest supplies no measured nurse-management dashboard case.

assumptions: The roster coordinator produces approved roster entries, finance staff post expenses and the unit coordinator records capacity in existing processes; their unchanged capture is outside this management review task.
Source contracts require unit identifier, period, roster coverage, expense amount and posting status; missing or misaligned fields remain manual review in s1.
The nurse manager captures contextual corrections and questions in retained s1 time; no newly structured staff concern feed is assumed.
Use existing reporting configuration first; no individual worker scoring, automatic allocation or new staff monitoring.
If reports are already aligned, savings are zero; external budget approval remains unchanged outside delegated decisions.
unknowns: Current report alignment and information assembly time
research_questions: Does a native unit-period view reduce assembly time after reconciliation and context checks?

already_counted.description: Interpretation and contextual checks remain counted.
Planning and staff management remain fully counted.

incremental.description: Manager validates changed report definitions and reconciles access changes.
Reporting administrator maintains unit and period mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=10+35+45=90; gross 10 less 2 focal upkeep gives net 8. High requires manual source alignment today; low covers already aligned reports or poor data. No staff conversation or managerial decision saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order and evaluate diagnostic tests within scope

steps.what: Assess the patient's condition and determine diagnostic test needs within authorised professional scope
outputs: supported test requirement or request for authorised clinician review

steps.what: Order permitted diagnostic tests or refer the request to an authorised practitioner
inputs: supported test requirement or request for authorised clinician review
outputs: authorised test order or escalated request

steps.what: Interpret and evaluate available diagnostic test results against the patient's condition and communicate conclusions
inputs: authorised test order or escalated request
outputs: documented evaluation and escalated clinical questions

tasks.design: Retain assessment, authorised ordering and result evaluation in the existing clinical system {OTHER}. No general diagnostic model or automatic test order is introduced; work beyond the nurse's authority remains with the authorised practitioner.
tasks.previous_blocker: A useful test decision and interpretation require clinical context and appropriate authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing ordering and results access support the task without a new inference system.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a relevant result from an incidental or unreliable finding.
tasks.human_edge: Relate evidence to the patient and recognise the need for specialist review.
tasks.altitude: Accountable test evaluation within professional scope.

reach.task: Resolve diagnostic questions beyond nursing authority
reach.learn: Which findings need further clinical interpretation

evidence.claim: Transpara's mammography capability is specialised and does not establish general nurse diagnostic test interpretation automation.

assumptions: Applicable professional scope and local authorisation are verified; the O*NET statement does not grant a generic nurse independent ordering authority.
The nurse produces the assessment and test requirement in s1 and captures the permitted order in s2; all decision and capture time remains.
Diagnostic service staff produce authorised results during separate testing; result production and collection are outside this task and unchanged.
No free structured diagnosis, autonomous test selection or new system upkeep is assumed.
unknowns: Actual nurse scope and ordering protocols
research_questions: Which tests can this nurse order and evaluate under the applicable authority?

already_counted.description: Assessment, ordering and evaluation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new diagnostic model or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero saving. Specialised imaging case results do not transfer to this broad task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend treatment or prescribe within authorised scope

steps.what: Assess treatment needs and review current medications, devices, patient goals and relevant clinical constraints
outputs: assessed treatment needs and unresolved concerns

steps.what: Recommend drugs, medical devices or therapeutic procedures, or prescribe only within explicit professional authority
inputs: assessed treatment needs and unresolved concerns
outputs: documented treatment recommendation or authorised prescription

tasks.design: Retain treatment assessment and recommendations with the nurse using the existing clinical record {OTHER}. Existing medication checks may support the process, but prescribing remains restricted to the worker's verified authority and no model chooses treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment choice depends on clinical context, patient goals and professional authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records and medication rules support current work without removing assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Balance competing treatment considerations and clarify uncertain or incomplete information.
tasks.human_edge: Understand patient needs and recognise the limits of the nurse's authority.

reach.learn: Which supporting observations are needed for a decision

evidence.claim: G-Standaard supports medication surveillance checks; it does not select treatment or grant prescribing authority.

assumptions: The nurse's actual prescribing authority must be verified; absent authority the output is a recommendation or escalated request.
The nurse produces assessed needs in s1 and captures the recommendation in s2; all assessment, discussion and capture time remains.
Existing clinicians and medication staff produce the current treatment record; no free reconciled medication list is introduced and clarification remains within retained time.
Existing rule checks are already in the baseline; no new model, autonomous prescribing or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Worker authority and local recommendation process
research_questions: Which treatment decisions belong to this nurse and which require a separate prescriber?

already_counted.description: Assessment and treatment recommendation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new treatment decision system or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work give zero saving. Current medication rules do not remove clinical assessment or recommendation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate infection control programs and precautions

steps.what: Review infection control concerns, current protocols and local conditions with responsible personnel
outputs: verified program concerns and consultation needs

steps.what: Direct or coordinate infection control programs and advise personnel about necessary precautions
inputs: verified program concerns and consultation needs
outputs: coordinated precaution actions and clarified responsibilities

tasks.design: Retain infection control coordination and consultation using approved protocols {DOCS} and current clinical records {OTHER}. No new surveillance model, generated precaution advice or automatic program decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols must be interpreted in local conditions and implemented through people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approved information supports consultation; a new drafting tool does not establish less coordination work.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve practical barriers and determine when specialist advice is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Understand local practice and secure clear responsibilities for precautions.
tasks.altitude: Practical and accountable infection control coordination.

reach.learn: Which local implementation barriers need specialist input

evidence.claim: Generic clinical documentation capabilities do not establish reduced infection control program coordination time.

assumptions: Clinical governance produces approved protocols, and care staff produce concern reports through existing processes.
The nurse verifies concerns and local context in s1 and clarifies actions and responsibilities in s2; all capture and consultation time remains.
No free structured infection flag, new surveillance feed or generated clinical advice is assumed.
Other personnel's implementation work remains unchanged outside the focal coordination baseline; no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Program scope, specialist access and existing escalation paths
research_questions: Which implementation barriers repeatedly require specialist consultation?

already_counted.description: Context review, coordination and advice remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new program system or content maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work yield zero saving. No invented surveillance administration or reduced consultation time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use verified management information while retaining clinical, managerial and infection control judgement.
reach: Refer decisions beyond scope to authorised practitioners
Resolve precautions with infection prevention specialists
role.ambitious_version: A nurse who uses reliable unit information and preserves accountable clinical and coordination decisions.
